articleTitle: Noise tube sources for mm wave FT spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Noise tubes in the wavelength region 6–4 mm, 3.3–2.1 mm and 2.1–1.36 mm are useful sources for millimeter wave Fourier Transform spectrometers. The output of the noise tubes has been adapted to the Michelson interferometer and the concentration optic of the pumped He cooled bolometer. Power comparison with the Mercury-Xenon lamp and power dependence of the noise tube on the driving currents has been studied. Plexiglas has been used as a long pass filter and the absorption coefficient measured.

articleTitle: A comparison of w-band free-space and waveguide dielectric property measurements
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two swept-frequency scalar techniques – free-space and in-waveguide – are compared for determining the complex dielectric constant of low-loss materials via measurement of their channel spectra. Factors such as measurement speed, low cost, good specimen statistics, complementarity, high-temperature suitability, and systematic errors are evaluated in this comparison. Data are presented as well as new theory for data reduction.

articleTitle: High-temperature dielectric measurements of high-purity alumina ceramics
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The speed of high-power (≥100 W) microwave sintering of ceramics from the ‘green’ state to the high-fired condition depends on the loss factor Ktan(δ). Free-space, W-band data at low power (≤0.1 mW) is presented on the complex dielectric constant of high-purity alumina (in air) in these two states – as achieved via conventional processing – for RT ≤ T ≤ 1700°C.

articleTitle: Complex permittivity of water between 0 and 30 thz
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A model of the complex permittivity for liquid water assumes a double-Debye relaxation model supplemented by two far-infrared resonance terms. The scheme is carried out by applying nonlinear least-squares fitting to the dielectric data reported below 30 THz.

articleTitle: Barrier-intrinsic-N+ (BIN) diodes for near-millimeter wave generation
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel class of structures which exhibit a highly nonlinear capacitance-voltage characteristic is introduced for application in the near-millimeter wave region.

articleTitle: Quantum well multipliers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A quantum well double barrier diode has been tested as a frequency tripler from 63.7 GHz to 191 GHz in a crossed waveguide mount designed for use with GaAs varactor diodes. Output power of 250 μw has been generated with an efficiency of 0.61 %. This performance is comparable to that obtained from a GaAs varactor diode with the same cutoff frequency.

articleTitle: Techniques for ceramic sintering using microwave energy
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The use of microwave energy for ceramic sintering offers exciting new possibilities for materials processing. Based on experience gathered in microwave processing associated with the heating of fusion plasmas, we have developed hardware and methods for uniformly heating ceramic parts of large volume and irregular shape to temperatures in excess of 1600°C, in vacuum or pressurized atmosphere. Microwave processing at 28 GHz yields enhanced densification rates with a corresponding reduction in sintering temperatures.

articleTitle: Design of an electronically tunable millimeter wave gyrotron backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A non-linear self-consistent computer simulation code is used to analyze the saturated output of the Gyrotron Backward Wave Oscillator (Gyro BWO) which can be used as a tunable driver for a 250 GHz FEL amplifier. Simulations show that the Gyrotron BWO using a Pierce/Wiggler gun configuration can produce at least 10 kW of microwave power over the range 249 GHz to 265 GHz by varying beam voltage alone.

articleTitle: An improved structure for subharmonically pumped millimeter-wave mixers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An improved structure for subharmonically pumped mixers is described. This structure is mechanically simple, and facilitates excellent mixer performance at millimeter-wave frequencies. A 183-GHz mixer built yields a mixer noise temperature as low as 900 K double sideband (DBS). The structure passed thermal and vibration tests for spaceborne applications.

articleTitle: A simplified method applied to various finline structures including dispersion, asymmetry, loss, finite strip thickness and discontinuity
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using a full wave analysis method, the effective dielectric constant, characteristic impedance, loss, finite strip thickness and step discontinuity of various finline structures were obtained. The transverse transmission line (TTL) method in the Fourier transform spectral domain, combined with the moment method, were used and may be applied to a variety of planar structures. Results are shown for general unilateral and bilateral finlines, including those with asymmetry in the E-plane of the rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: Planar matching of antennas on electrically thick dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of matching printed circuit antennas on electrically thick substrates to air using simple matching layers of dielectrics. Radiation patterns have been calculated for several different layered structures illustrating their effects on power radiated by slot antennas.

articleTitle: Analysis of mode competition including mismatch effect of window
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A mode competition is one of the most important problems in designing a TEOn gyrotron, which is affected by the presence of an output window as well as a cavity design. When the gyrotron has a single disc alumina window, its bandwidth is so narrow that competing modes, i.e. TE2n modes can not completely propagate through the window[l][2]. Wave reflection at the window would increases an effective external Q value and deforms an axial RF profile in a cavity so as to lower a start-oscillation threshold of TE2n modes and cause a severe mode competition.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional horn imaging arrays
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A two-dimensional horn imaging array has been demonstrated at 242 GHz. In this configuration, a dipole is suspended in a pyramidal horn on a 1-μm silicon-oxynitride membrane. This approach leaves room for low-frequency lines and processing electronics. Pattern measurements agree well with theory, and show no sidelobes and 3-dB beamwidth of 35° and 46° for the E and H planes respectively. Possible application areas include superconducting tunnel-junction receivers for radio astronomy and imaging arrays for plasma diagnostics and radiometry.

articleTitle: Symmetric and non-symmetric modes in a 200 kw, 100 GHz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have published a few papers on the development of a 100 GHz 200 kW Gyrotron oscillator aiming at producing at least 20,000 pulses with 90 % mode purity.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence and sample variation of dielectric properties in a commercial low loss alumina grade
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A batch of a low loss alumina (AL23) was analyzed at 9.4–12.0, 30–40, 140 and 380 GHz for variations in permittivity and dielectric loss tangents. Classifying the permittivity values, the batch could be split up into two groups with ∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>‘ = 9.67 and 9.70, respectively. No correlation to mass density was established. Sample variation was still more pronounced for dielectric loss, with an evident relationship to the permittivity groups only at X band and Ka band frequencies. In contrast to ∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>‘, tan 8 depends strongly on frequency, rising from ∼ 1.10–4 at 10 GHz to ∼ 10.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> at 380 GHz.

articleTitle: A high power gyrotron oscillator at 8 GHz
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the frame of a development program aiming towards an 8 GHz, 500 kW CW gyrotron, a 200 kW prototype has been tested at pulse lengths up to 30 ms, yielding 50% electronic efficiency. More than 99% of the output power were measured in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode. A fully-cooled long pulse gyrotron for 300 kW at maximum efficiency (57.8%) has been manufactured.

articleTitle: System study of a millimeter wave debris tracking radar
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 35 GHz radar system has been studied for space debris tracking. The objective is to track the particles ranging in size from 1 mm to SO mm up to a range of 25 km. The system requires various state-of-the-art technologies including phased array, monopulse tracking, pulse compression, high power transmitter and pulse integration.

articleTitle: A full band 18–225 GHz scalar network analyzer
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A Millimeter Scalar Network Analyzer (MSNA), based on a new concept, permits to cover the whole 18-225 GHz interval without any drawer to change, and avoiding the problem of the many expensive sources usually needed. Transmission measurements are performed very easily at any frequency within minutes, with a dynamic range over 6odB up to 160 GHz, and above 40 dB up to 225 GHz. Small power attenuation changes (down to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>) can be detected when applying an external modulation. Many applications concern the test of various millimeter components (wave guides, attenuators, cavities, antennas…), the characterization of materials (dielectrics…), the spectroscopy of solids, atoms and molecules.

articleTitle: Dielectric waveguide branching directional coupler
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A dielectric waveguide branching directional coupler with curved transitions is presented and investigated by the method, which combines the building block approach of multimode network theory with rigorous mode matching procedure. The coupling problem is analyzed in terms of the scattering of incident surface wave by the nonuniform dielectric structure as a whole. Particular attention is directed to the effect of radiation due to bending of the curved transition waveguides on the performances of the coupler. Numerical results are given to establish useful guidelines for the design of directional couplers.

articleTitle: A microstrip tripler to 47 GHz
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a planar microstrip millimeter-wave tripler to 47 GHz fabricated on an alumina substrate and using a commercially available varactor diode. Unlike waveguide multipliers the microstrip tripler can be directly-integrated with an FET DRO. The tripler provides +12 dBm output power which is ample to drive a typical millimeter-wave mixer.

articleTitle: Planar antennas on thick dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two types of frequency independent planar antennas on thick dielectrics, the log-spiral and log-periodic, have been designed, fabricated and characterized at millimeter wave frequencies. Measured beam patterns displayed beam widths and side lobe angles comparable to theory, and increasing the number of terminals produced similar patterns.

articleTitle: Influence of transit time effects on the optimum design and maximum oscillation frequency of quantum well oscillators
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Due to the inherently fast transport associated with tunneling, resonant tunneling diodes have been proposed for use in extremely high frequency oscillators. Transit time effects in these oscillators should be considered and can be exploited to improve their rf performance, as in a quantum well injection transit time (QWITT) diode. Small and large signal analyses of these transit time effects are presented, and their implications on the optimum design and maximum possible oscillation frequency of quantum well oscillators is discussed.

articleTitle: False alarm and detection probability factors and their implementation on lidar design
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A statistical model has been developed for the analysis and design of Laser Radar systems (LIDAR). A set of equations, developed for conventional Radar systems, was reconfigured and adapted to the optical case. The analysis and the related developed set of equations were dedicated to the case of detecting co-operative retro reflector carrying targets against background which is a composition of clutter, noise and backscatter sources. The equations developed were evaluated against realisitic system and atmospheric conditions presenting the relations between detection and false alarms probabilities and effective range. This method is very useful in evaluation and design of LIDAR Systems.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave microstrip integrated circuit transceiver packaging
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There has been considerable progress 1n the development of millimeter-wave hybrid integrated circuits. In program applications where low-cost and high-volume producibility are the key factors, planar microstrip technology 1s the preferred approach. The design and packaging of three fully integrated microstrip FMCW transceivers operating at 35, 60, and 94 GHz are discussed, plus a discussion on a unique low-cost, low-mass packaging approach for millimeter-wave microstrip based systems.

articleTitle: Cyclotron autoresonant maser (carm) ec heating source for high field tokamaks
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent theoretical work has found conditions for stable operation of a CARM amplifier<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. The magnetic field should be somewhat less than β<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> = Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> for stability, but considerably greater than the gyro-TWT grazing condition for higher efficiency due to autoresonance and higher frequency due to a Doppler upshift. The design of a 3 MW, 560 GHz CARM amplifier is presented.

articleTitle: Laser and photodetector packages for microwave optical transmission
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Optoelectronic packages for microwave diode lasers and PIN photodiodes have been developed that preserve RF integrity of the devices to beyond 15 GHz, provide effective optical coupling to single-mode fiber, and, in the case of the laser, thermally stabilize operation over wide ambient conditions.

articleTitle: A mm-wave electrically controlled dielectric waveguide phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new concept of electrically controlled phase shifter has been designed, realized and tested at laboratory level. This device makes use of an insulated dielectric waveguide whose conductor plate is a metallized piezoelectric actuator. Through appropriate biasing of this actuator, the mean distance between the dielectric rod and the conductor plate is changed, thus modifying the guided wavelength. Both efficiency and figure of merit of such device make it attractive in the mm-wave band; design criteria are presented, and prototype testing is compared with theoretical results.

articleTitle: A producible 94 GHz detector circuit for large-scale vidicon applications
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Described is a 94 GHz diode detector circuit/antenna element which employs a 700 GHz f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">co</inf> GaAs Schottky diode fabricated with a fully planar, ion implantation process for high yield, uniformity, and repeatability. This was developed as a single “pixel” for a large focal plane array containing thousands of such elements fabricated on a number of large GaAs chips (“tiles”). Measured 94 GHz current sensitivity was 3–4 μA/μW with TSS of −50 dBm (BW=1MHz).

articleTitle: 183 GHz monolithic subharmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes the design and optimisation of a rugged, 183 GHz, subharmonic mixer using a novel monolithic integrated circuit. The circuit consists of two, balanced planar GaAs Schottky-Barrier diodes symmetrically opposed together with associated antenna coupling structures.

articleTitle: Far-forward scattering from a tokamak piasma with a tunable gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: GYROTRON III (1) can provide more than 10 W of cw power over the frequency range 75 to 330 GHz. It has been used as a source in a millimeter-wave far-forward scattering experiment to observe scattering from density fluctuations associated with Mirnov oscillations in the department's TORTUS tokamak (2).

articleTitle: The general equations of ir systems' acquisition and tracking range
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The wellknown IR systems' acquisition and tracking range equations are derived only upon the null space background condition. In this paper, the general range equations are derived. When the background effect can be neglected, they simplify to the previous equations; on the general condition, from the equations derived here, we can obtain more correct results about acquisition and tracking range.

articleTitle: Gyrotron thomson scattering diagnostics of ions in D-T burning tokamaks
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Collective Thomson scattering can be used to diagnose localized ion temperature as well as alpha particle velocity distribution and density in a D-T burning tokamak. With one diagnostic beam a simultaneous, but independent, measure of the bulk ion temperature and alpha particle parameters can be made. Use of a long pulse, millimeter-wave gyrotron offers a significant margin in signal to noise ratio capability (√Δfτ > 1,000) not previously possible with lasers.

articleTitle: Optically controlled millimeter wave phased arrays: Status and future challenges
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Various optical techniques are under consideration to provide signal distribution for GaAs MMIC radiating elements in large phased array antennas, to reduce weight, complexity and electrical interference. In this presentation, system architectures concepts for optically controlled phased arrays are outlined. The key optical and microwave components required for the feasibility of these architectures for millimeter wave range are described.

articleTitle: New compact quasi-periodic and aperiodic mode converters for 60 and 140 GHz gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: New shorter, broader bandwidth designs are discussed for TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> varying-radius mode converters and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> serpentine mode converters for a 2.779 cm diameter circular waveguide at 60 and 140 GHz. Designs combining TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on-1</inf> converters and a 6.35–2.779 cm taper are also presented.

articleTitle: Second harmonic 106.4 GHz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A second harmonic gyrotron was designed and constructed for operation at 106.4 GHz, 100 kw peak output power, utilizing a TE021/TE031 complex cavity. Design calculation results for 80 kV 8 A operation are presented. Initial tube tests have been carried out. Peak output powers of 120 kW have been achieved.

articleTitle: Design of a high power, 140 GHz carm amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A high-power, 140 GHz cyclotron autoresonance maser (CARM) amplifier experiment is planned at M.I.T. The experiment will employ a high-voltage (450–700 kV) electron beam from a Pierce gun and a helical wiggler to produce the required β<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊤</inf> on the beam. Details of the design and predicted performance will be presented. One- and three-dimensional computer simulation results are presented and the influence of velocity spread on CARM operation is discussed.

articleTitle: Optical electronic characterization of monolithic millimeter-wave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) has been measured using a picosecond optical sampling technique. The broadband signals at the input and output of the MMIC are sampled using photoconductive switches. The spectral response of the MMIC is analyzed and compared with the continuous wave (CW) characteristics.

articleTitle: Experimental performance of an optically controlled coplanar waveguide phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Preliminary measurements on an optically controlled coplanar waveguide phase-shifter are presented. The device is based on the interaction between the wave propagating on the transmission line and an optically induced plasma in the CPW semiconductor substrate. A prototype device consisting of a Schottky contacted CPW on a heterostructure AlGaAs/GaAs/AlGaAs/ S.I. GaAs substrate was tested. The preliminary measurements show that optical control of the phase is possible, even at low illumination intensities.

articleTitle: V-groove guide and components for 100 GHz operation
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper gives the theoretical and experimental work on the guide and the developed components, which include transitions, bends, couplers and junctions. A conformal mapping technique has been applied to grooves of V-shaped cross-section. Experimental measurements confirm the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: 3-D ribbon beams for gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Three dimensional codes, developed to simulate high density, high energy ribbon beams to be used in gyrotrons are presented. A 3-D Pierce type gun using plane boundaries and a MIG type gun with arbitrary boundary electrodes are analyzed by solving the three dimensional Poisson's equation subject to the given geometrical boundary conditions using finite difference technique. Results of the numerical solutions as well as some initial experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Frequency measurement of FIR laser lines of metrological and astrophysical interest
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The optically pumped FIR lasers are the most convenient sources of CW radiation in the 1 THz to 6 THz region. The frequency stability and reproducibility (a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>) makes the FIR lasers a source suitable as a local oscillator for high sensitivity heterodyne spectrometers of astrophysical interest, and as a stable oscillator for Stark and Zeeman intracavity spectroscopy. Moreover the fine structure atomic transitions in the far infrared have a considerable practical interest. As an example, the fine structure transitions between the metastable triplet levels <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> of Magnesium and Calcium, at 0.6, 1.2, 1.5, and 3.1 THz respectively, are of relevant metrological interest, because they can be used as a reference for a new kind of absolute atomic frequency standards [1,2]; while the N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> – <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> transition, which has recently been measured in the laboratory by Cooksy et al. [3], is of particular interest from an astronomical point of view. The discovery of this transition in the interstellar medium seems to be possible, at least in principle.

articleTitle: A new optoelectronic continuous wave millimeter-wave source
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using picosecond photoconductors switched by a mode-locked laser along with filters and amplifiers, we were able to create an optically-synchronized 20 GHz wave.

articleTitle: Inter-injection locking — a novel phase control technique for monolithic phased arrays
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel technique for phase control in millimeter-wave phased arrays has been demonstrated with a 10 GHz model. The main beam of a four-element array has been steered ±5° using only one phase shifter. The system's characteristics such as an effective radiated power of 7.4 W, a sidelobe level 16 dB below the main beam, and adaptability to monolithic fabrication make this technique attractive for beam steering at millimeter wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of the high efficiency 127 μm FIR laser line of 13CD3OH and other 13CD3OH, CD3OH, CD3OD, CH3OH and 13CH3OH FIR laser lines
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An assignment is proposed for the strong 127.02 μm FIR line in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH pumped with very high efficiency by the 10P(8) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser line. Other assignments and predictions are also discussed for CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH, CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH and CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OD FIR lines.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave attenuation and delay for a fog event
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Atmospheric propagation effects of suspended water droplets (SWD) representing haze, fog, or cloud conditions are modeled for frequencies f up to about 1000 GHz. The Rayleigh approximation is used to formulate SWD propagation effects and a double-Debye relaxation model is applied to predict frequency and temperature characteristics of the permittivity for water. Experimental results of fog attenuation and differential delay at 50.4, 81.8, 140.7, 245.5 GHz over a 0.81 km propagation path are applied to test the model.

articleTitle: A nodular approach to beam waveguide — the optiguidetm system
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have developed a compact system of Gaussian beam waveguide using low loss lenses which is useful for test bench as well as subsystem applications. The frequency range from 75 GHz (4mm wavelength) to 300 GHz (1mm wavelength) is covered in octave bandwidths. Optiguide<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> Gaussian beam waveguide can handle multiple polarizations, and can be adapted to handle multiple spatial modes as well. To date, we have developed 3- and 4-port directional couplers, attenuators, isolators, and circulators. Polarization processing components include grids which can act as polarization diplexers or analyzers, half-wave plates, and quarter-wave plates. The modular approach readily lends itself to configuring of systems to provide a wide range of functions. Some data on a 140–220 GHz (WR-5 waveguide band) system are presented,

articleTitle: Stimulated emission, amplification, and upward frequency shift of the orbitron maser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Orbitron Maser is a device in which R.F. radiation is produced by electrons in elongated or circular orbits around a positively charged central anode wire. This wire is surrounded by a circular cylinder which is at ground potential. This cylinder acts both as a cathode and as a cavity resonator. articleTitle: Far infrared excitations of shallow donor impurities in gaas/algaas multiple quantum well heterostructures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The effects of confinement of impurities (acceptors and donors) in semiconductors of reduced dimensionality been the focus of much recent theoretical (1) and experimental (2) attention. In the present work, far infrared (FIR) and resonant Raman scattering (RRS) experiments have been performed on MBE-grown GaAs/AlGaAs multiple quantum well heterostructures that were selectively doped with Si donors in the centers of the quantum well and barrier layers. Motivations for these investigations include a need to obtain information on the binding of electrons in the well to positively charged impurities in the barriers and to examine in detail the effects of the screening of the Coulomb interaction by free carriers in this quasi two-dimensional system. Representative results of these studies are highlighted below.

articleTitle: Development of high efficiency frequency multipliers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A frequency multiplier combined with a fundamental solid state oscillator is an attractive choice for the local oscillator of a low noise mm- or submm-receiver in space applications. A Schottky diode in the varactor mode provides the best multiplier element up to 500 GHz and in the varistor mode from 500 to 800 GHz. At 100 GHz efficiencies as high as 45 % for a doubler and 28 % for a tripler have been demonstrated experimentally at the Helsinki University of Technology. A stacked GaAs p-n varactor and a GaAs resonant tunneling (quantum well) diode are new interesting multiplication elements for mm-waves.

articleTitle: Infrared radio-frequency double resonance in ch3od
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Ten infrared radio-frequency double resonance signals have been observed in CH3OD. Tentative assignments of these transitions will be discussed. The observed transitions belong to A-type symmetry states and allow for the determination of asymmetry splitting parameters. These are useful in further assignments of rovibrational lines belonging to the CO-stretch fundamental band, which has recently been recorded.

articleTitle: A gyroresonant phase filter for the enhancement of traveling wave gain and efficiency
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The growth rate and efficiency of a general traveling wave interaction (TWI) can be significantly enhanced by selectively suppressing those electrons which are phased to gain energy from the wave. We have observed in simulations of a particular TWI, a cyclotron autoresonant maser (CARM), the increase of efficiency by a factor of three and growth rate by two.

articleTitle: Parasitic effects on millimeter-wave phase shifter design
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The parasitic effects on millimeter-wave phase shifters have been studied for both analog and digital applications. The analog phase shifter uses the hybrid coupled configuration and the digital phase shifter uses the loaded line configuaraton. The results have shown that the parasitics have strong effects on the phase shifter performance at high frequencies.

articleTitle: Electrostatically pumped cross-field free electron laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We report experimental and theoretical studies of a novel type of cross-field microwave generator. The cathode is smooth while the anode is rippled (Fig.1) to produce an azimuthally periodic modulation of the radial electric field (analogous to an electrostatic wiggler). The system is operated in the inverted geometry,<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> where electrons are field-emitted from the inside of the smooth outer conductor. The depth of the grooves is adjusted so as to favor FEL interactions and minimize the usual slow-wave (magnetron) interactions.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Approximate analytic single-particle orbits in the external crossed uniform electric and magnetic fields and the radial electric wiggler field of an idealized planar device are obtained. These orbits provide a basis for uniform and nonuniform kinetic and fluid equilibrium distribution functions. These equilibria in turn provide a basis for linear stability analyses of the device, which yield appropriate dispersion relations. Experimentally, we observe for our parameters (V ∼ 300 kV, I ∼ 1 kA, B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‖</inf> ∼ 5 kG, N = 0,8,12,24 wiggler periods) a high power microwave signal in the Ka-band. Removal of the wiggler (smooth-bore magnetron configuration) results in a reduction of the signal by ∼ 20 dB. These results suggest an emission mechanism analogous to that of the rippled-field magnetron.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>

articleTitle: Far-infrared spectroscopy of the n2–ar alloy
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Hydrogen, nitrogen and methane have been extensively studied in the last two decades as the simplest examples of molecular solids characterized by anisotropic interactions: at low temperature oH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> exhibit transitions to various orientationally ordered phases, whose structures are depending upon pressure. Such orientational order may be destroyed by the addition of spherical-potential impurities, like p-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Ar, and Kr, respectively. Neutron scattering and NMR have been widely used to investigate these alloys of molecular solids, with particular regard to the possible existence of orientational glass-like phases at low temperature (1–4). Far-infrared spectroscopy was employed nearly exclusively on the oH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-pH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> system (5).

articleTitle: The open-cavity millimeter-wave resonator as a high-Q microstrip circuit element
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The need for narrow-percentage-bandwidth filters, efficient power combiners, and other circuits requiring high-Q resonant elements becomes increasingly difficult to satisfy above 30 GHz. Even the classical waveguide-cavity approaches become less useful at millimeter wavelengths because of extremely critical machining tolerances and fundamental limitations imposed by skin-effect losses. The fabrication convenience of planar integrated circuits is far outweighed by the even poorer maximum Q's obtainable in microstrip or stripline. Although dielectric resonators have mitigated this problem to some degree, they are difficult to use at millimeter wavelengths because of the small dimensions and critical positioning required.

articleTitle: Probing semiconductor superlattice transport by submillimeter wave cyclotron resonance
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Cyclotron resonance with the magnetic field oriented perpendicular to the growth direction is shown to be an effective probe of vertical transport in semiconductor superlattices. For small magnetic fields the experiments directly measure the mini-band mass and scattering rate. At large magnetic fields, when the cyclotron diameter is comparable to the superlattice period, we have a rare opportunity to examine Landau states in a periodic potential in a magnetic field when the effective mass approximation is no longer applicable. Under these conditions we can resolve resonances from different parts of the superlattice unit cell.

articleTitle: Pump-free crossed-field free-electron laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Starting from basic concepts, we propose a new kind of free-electron laser(FEL) : the pump-free crossed-field FEL in which the condition E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> + V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>xB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> =0 is not satisfied, and the electron orbit without radiation fields and undulator or wiggler fields is not straight line (in planar configuration). In the fluid dynamical analysis without taking account of the space charge effect, FEL instability is found near resonance Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">±1–</inf>kz<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>=0, while no FEL instability near resonance Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>-kz<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>+± √1-β<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">za</inf> Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>=0.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave science and technology at very low temperatures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Above helium temperatures, the photon energy hv in the millimeter region is significantly less than the thermal energy kT. The opposite is true in the optical region. This paper first discusses a newly developed technique that makes possible the study of gas phase systems at temperatures ≤ 4K, a regime where phenomena in the millimeter wave region can take on many of the properties of optical science and technology. Then, with gas phase molecular systems as the example, the temperature dependence of electromagnetic interactions is explored. Finally some experimental results from this low temperature regime are presented and additional research opportunities discussed.

articleTitle: Reliable, high power, passive ka band receiver protection
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper discusses the design of Ka Band Receiver Protectors for use up to 80KW. The unique design offers full passive protection, controlled phase performance and high reliability. The design has been proven in full system operation.

articleTitle: Submillimiter measurement of high electron mobility transistors
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Cyclotron Resonance measurements are used to determine the effective masses for High Electron Mobility Transistors. The effective mass is a function of gate voltage.

articleTitle: Submillimeter wave inverse smith-purcell effect
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have observed the inverse Smith-Purcell (ISP) effect for the first time by using a submillimeter wave laser as a driving source. The ISP effect is one of the candidates for laser-driven linacs with a metallic grating as an interaction circuit to produce acceleration gradient of a few GeV/m. In this paper, we describe our experimental apparatus including newly developed CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser and the first experimental evidence of this effect.

articleTitle: Synchrotron radiation as a light source in the submillimeter and millimeter wave regions
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A high pressure mercury are lamp has been used as a useful light source in the far-infrared region since the beginning of this century. Effort has been made to improve the spectroscopic method rather than the light source. In fact, long wavelength spectroscopy has been advanced mainly by the development of techniques of Fourier transform interferometry and of the low temperature detector.

articleTitle: High power submillimeter gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: High power, submillimeter gyrotron oscillator experiments are presently being conducted at M.I.T. These experiments are designed to operate at second harmonic and generate output powers up to 100 kW for 1 μsec pulses. To achieve second harmonic emission three different cavity configurations have been explored, a tapered cavity, a slotted cavity, and a cavity with an output iris. In the last cavity, second harmonic emission was observed at 301 GHz and 339 GHz, with output powers of 4-6 kW.

articleTitle: Investigation of finiine strip discontinuities and its application to millimeter wave filters
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Up to now the finlines proposed by Meier as MMW transmission line for fMW integrated circuits have been used by components designers with growing interest and importance. There has been an increasing activity concerning the theoretical foundations of the discontinuities of finlines in order to lead eventually to a more sophisticated CAD program of printed E-plane circuits. But only few research has been carried out for the general case when the fin slot is less than the height of housing.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1,2]</sup> The results are emperical or approximate. No rigorous results are available. In this paper the general case of finline strip discontinuities is first investigated rigorously by resonance method and variational technique and a set of design charts are evaluated. Using these results Ka-band band pass filters with unilateral and bilateral finline strips have been realised demonstrating the feasibility of the employed equivalent circuit approach. The measured results agree well with the theoretical predictions. The measured minimum insertion losses at pass band are 0.64 dB and 0. 52 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Induced magnetic perturbations by plasma heating
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We discuss the possible induction of magnetic field fluctuations in laboratory plasma during plasma heating by electromagnetic waves. Basically, the electromagnetic wave excited lower hybrid waves may become pump waves to excite instabilities. We will describe a process that can simultaneously generate plasma density fluctuations and magnetic field fluctuations. Significant cross-field magnetic perturbations can be produced and, then, give rise to the plasma confinement problem during plasma heating.

articleTitle: Solid state local oscillator sources for millimeter and sub-millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper presents performance data for state-of-the-art Gunn devices used as local oscillators in the 30 to 150 GHz frequency range. Different methods of oscillator design are discussed, including fixed frequency Gunn oscillators, and frequency multipliers driven by Gunn oscillators. Performance tradeoffs between output power, frequency stability, noise, size, and power consumption are analyzed and correlated with experimental data for fixed frequency sources.

articleTitle: Relativistic cyclotron maser driven by an intense electron beam generator with 0.4 μs pulselength
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We present high power microwave emission data from an electron cyclotron maser device driven by a long pulse (0.4 μs), high current (0.5-1 kA), relativistic (< 0.4–0.5 MV) electron beam generator. An open waveguide resonator with a single circular iris was employed in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> circular mode interacting with an annular electron beam generated by a velvet cathode. Results demonstrate that peak microwave power in excess of 0.6 MW can be achieved with peak electronic efficiencies in the range of 6 percent for injected currents less than 100 A. Frequency chirping upward through 7 GHz has been measured, corresponding to the drooping beam voltage. High power cyclotron maser emission has been maintained over 0.2 μs to 0.3 μs, limited primarily by generator voltage droop due to plasma diode closure. Observed rapid, spiky modulation of the microwave output power resembles mode locking behavior in conventional lasers.

articleTitle: Information enhancement of high resolution mm-wave images
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Images of an airborne, scanning, radiomeeter operating at a frequency of 98 GHz, have been analyzed. The goal of this study was to develop algorithms to enhance the information content of these images and make their interpretation easier for an observer. Nonlinear transform techniques have been applied for grey-scale modification, noise reduction, edge enhancement and deconvolution. Results of these algorithms on selected mm-wave images will be presented.

articleTitle: Analyses of picosecond pulse propagation along a coupled slotline on a lossy multilayer integrated circuit substrate
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Picosecond ultra high speed pulse propagation along a coupled slotline integrated on a lossy multilayer substrate is investigated by full wave spectral domain analysis with improved accuracy. The theoretical results based on both even and odd mode excitations of a coupled slotline are presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wavelength Bolometers Cooled by Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have constructed composite bolometers operating at temperatures near 0.1 K to detect one millimeter continuum radiation. Our most sensitive detector has a measured electrical noise equivalent power (NEP) of 7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−17</sup> W Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>, which is about three times more sensitive than previously reported. We present our experimental results, and design considerations for 0.1 K bolometers.

articleTitle: Twelve channel ECE diagnostic system of the new wendelstein stellarator W VII-AS
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: WENDELSTEIN VII-AS is a modular stellarator with 5 toroidal field periods, an aspect ratio of 10 and a large radius of 2 m. It is an upgrade version of the 1985 shut down W VII-A using twisted coils instead of main field coils and helical windings forming an optimized magnetic configuration. Main design guidelines for the advanced stellarator concept have been the minimization of parallel currents and of deviations of particles from the magnetic surfaces which leads to higher plasma equilibrium pressure and a reduction of transport losses. The experiment is scheduled to become operational in late 1987.

articleTitle: Mode competition in a complex cavity for gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: One of the advantages of a complex cavity is the possibility of suppression of parasitic modes by a properly chosen geometry. However, due to nonlinear dynamical effects other modes can be excited and, possibly, ruin the expected advantage mentioned. We study the conditions of self excitation of parasitic modes in the presence of oscillations of the operating mode. Detailed results are presented for a complex cavity with the mode conversion TE03/TE06 planned for the KfK experiment.

articleTitle: Invited keynote possibilities for microwave/far infrared cavities and waveguides using high temperature superconductors
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Possibilities for use of high temperature superconductors in microwave/far infrared resonators and waveguides are described. Relative to conventional superconductors, the use of high temperature superconductors could remove the constraint of relatively low energy gaps and provide larger thermal margins and more effective cooling. The higher critical magnetic fields may also be important for an increased range of operation. These features could be used to improve performance of present superconducting microwave cavities and to provide new applications at both microwave frequencies and at much higher frequencies. Constraints that may inhibit development include a need for superconducting properties over a high fraction of the surface, limits on critical RF fields and the effect of D.C. magnetic fields.

articleTitle: The modified equations of a multielement parallel scanning imaging systems Δf and netd
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a multielement parallel scanning infrared imaging systems and shows that the instantaneous field of view determined by the y-direetion center space of the adjacent sensitive area is a important parameter for calculating the systems noise equivalent, bandwidth, and designing a two-dimensional scanning system. The limited and inaccurate calculations of the systems noise equivalent bandwidth, in previous article are pointed out and the new calculation equations given in this paper are available.

articleTitle: A new technique for raising operating frequency of pin diodes
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two new types of integrated switch are presented. Conmercial beam-lead diode originally designed for lower frequency band can be used at higher frequency band by means of reverse-mode and compensation technique. The experimental results of two prototype circuits at Ka-band and W-band are given.

articleTitle: Large signal modeling of millimeter wave gunn diodes for planar circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A simple and accurate experimental technique is described to determine the equivalent circuit parameters of millimeter wave (30–100 GHz) GaAs and InP Gunn diodes under large signal conditions for a planar microstrip circuit. The modeling has resulted in the development of microstrip oscillators and VCOs with excellent agreement between measured and calculated performance.

articleTitle: Modeling of collisional energy transfer in optically pumped far infrared lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Optically pumped far infrared (OPFIR) lasers have been the subject of extensive theoretical and experimental investigations. A detailed review of this work has been published recently (1). Although many important aspects of these lasers are now well understood, comprehensive modeling of these lasers is very difficult because of the large number of states that influence the lasing and because of potentially nonlinear and inhomogeneous effects of the pump laser. Consequently numerous approximations and simplifications have been required to obtain tractable analytic models. An additional complication has been a lack of the requisite extensive experimental data needed to guide the development of these models. The net effect has been models that extrapolate poorly into new operating regimes (e.g. pump intensity and pressure) and derived parameters that are related to actual physical processes in complicated or unknown ways.

articleTitle: A new submillimetre-wave detector using cyclotron resonance in ga1-xalxas/gaas heterostructures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have shown that a Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>As/GaAs heterostructure can be used as a sensitive tunable detector of mm-wave/sübmm-wave radiation. The mechanism for detection requires the application of a magnetic field varying from approximately 0.2T at 94GHz (3.2mm wavelength) to 6.2T at 2500GHz (119μm wavelength). The speed of such a detector could be several orders of magnitude greater than comparable InSb detectors.

articleTitle: Mode control in an overmoded gyrotron oscillator via priming
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Control of axial modes is accomplished in a gyrotron oscillator by injection of an external signal into the oscillator. It is found that the external signal need be present only during the initial stages of the pulsed oscillator buildup. It is also noted that the oscillation is not phase locked, due to the low input power level. From these two facts it is seen that priming is the mechanism responsible for the mode control effect. An analysis of the priming phenomenon is made using a quasi-linear theory (in the mode amplitudes) to understand the dependence of the degree of mode control on the external power level.

articleTitle: Atf ech waveguide component development and testing
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Advanced Toroidal Facility (ATF) Electron Cyclotron Heating (ECH) system presently under construction will consist of two 53.2-GHz, 200-kW continuous-wave (cw) gyrotrons with a mode-controlled waveguide system and polarized launcher optimized for maximum power in the ATF plasma. Several components, such as a waveguide mode-analyzing directional coupler, a TiO2 mode absorber, miter bends, and a polarization-selectable beamed launcher, have been developed and tested. Laboratory results and initial high-power operation of the system are presented.

articleTitle: A comparison at infrared wavelengths of metal-grating and dielectric-film free-electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A comparison of the tuning, gain, saturation, and beam-quality-related restrictions of metal-grating and dielectric-film free-electron lasers will be presented. While recent operation of the former has resulted in tunable radiation in the low mm wavelength band, indications are that the device may readily be scaled to operate at submm, far-infrared, and possibly shorter wavelengths. For the latter, operation to date has been well into the FIR. These results, and an in depth look at the prospects of the metal-grating FEL, will also be summarized.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic search for the floppy-rigid transition in bulk se1–x gex glasses
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: No transitions occur in the room temperature longitudinal and transverse elastic constants of Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> glasses up to × = 0.30. The transverse elastic constant appears to saturate near × = 0.25. These results contradict a random network model for these glasses which predicts a transition at ×<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> =0.20, but they are not inconsistent with a molecular cluster model.

articleTitle: A small tunable optically pumped far infrared laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A small diameter CW FIR laser that can provide approximately 100 MHz spectrally pure tunability has been developed and studied both experimentally and theoretically (1). Operation of this laser at pressures significantly greater than the maximum allowed by previously accepted theory yields the large tunability. The new model includes additional high energy vibrational states and appropriate energy transfer mechanisms that fundamentally alter the behavior in the high pressure, high pump intensity regime. Although <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F is used for both the experimental demonstration and the theoretical model, the concept is general and should apply to all diffusion deactivated FIR lasers.

articleTitle: A novel method of measuring the dielectric properties at 100 GHz using a groove-guide resonator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Taking advantages of the low loss and open nature of the groove guide and relatively cheap linear transducers, a simple technique has been developed to measure the dielectric properties at 100 GHz using a groove-guide resonator. The change of frequency or length to restore resonance before and after the insertion of the dielectric and the change of the respective Q-factor can be used to compute both the permittivity and loss-tangent.

articleTitle: Intermodal tuning behavior of an etalon tuned slm tea-co2 laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Interference fringes produced by an extra-cavity wedged etalon and recorded with a 128-element pyroelectric detector array have been used to study the mode structure and fine-tuning behavior of a TEA-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser, which is tuned with a diffraction grating and a temperature controlled intracavity etalon (1). The TEA-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser can be tuned over a range of about ± 2 GHz centered on each of its strong emission lines, and its longitudinal mode spacing is ∼120 MHz. The wedge and detector array provide an experimental resolution of a few 10's of MHz so that the intermode spacing of the laser can be probed in several well-resolved steps. As the temperature of the intracavity etalon is changed, the fine-scale tuning curve of the laser is a staircase function, with a series of flat (nearly constant frequency) segments separated by sharp jumps to the next longitudinal mode frequency. Oscilloscope traces recorded with a photon drag detector show the laser pulses to alternate, as the frequency scan proceeds, between pure single longitudinal mode structure and a small admixture of a second longitudinal mode. These results will be discussed in the context of the development of a high-power multi-atmosphere continuously-tunable SLM CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser (2).

articleTitle: Cd0.2hg0.8te epi—layer for a high detectivity pc—type ir detector
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: High quality n-type Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>Hg <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Te epi-layers doped with In below 0.1 ppm, whose carrier concentration and mobility at 77 K are below 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> and over 2× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V·S, respectively, have been grown by LPE on CdTe (111) B substrates with EPDs below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. A new result obtained is that long carrier diffusion length is essentially important for realizing a high performance detector, whose detectivity reaches to D∗BLIP.

articleTitle: Analysis of the propagation properites in an inverted strip dielectric guide
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The inverted strip dielectric guide (ISDG) is a variant of image guide. The structure consists of a guiding layer with dielectric constant ∊r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> placed on dielectric strip ∊r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> which in turn rests on a ground plane, where ∊r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> > ∊r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.

articleTitle: Orotron oscillators at mm-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The principles of operation of Orotrons (Ledatrons) based on the Smith-Purcell effect in an optical resonant cavity are presented, and experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Material requirements for gyrotron windows
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A typical double disc window geometry is described for a CW millimeter-wave gyrotron. The desired microwave and mechanical properties for the two discs and for the coolant material are discussed. Sample thermal and mechanical calculations are presented for a 200 kW CW 60 GHz window design. The measured peak temperature for the same window is given for comparison.

articleTitle: Ch3oh laser lines assignments and frequency predictions by transition loops
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH line frequencies obtained from the diagonalization of a theoretical Hamiltonian are affected by inaccuracies of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> or higher, the inaccuracy increasing with the value of the quantum numbers involved in the transition. The inaccuracy on lines involving vibrationally excited levels, like, for instance, the lasing lines, is usually higher than the inaccuracy on the absorption lines within the vibrational ground state.

articleTitle: Ka-band hybrid integrated circuit mutually injection locked power combined VCO
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a novel, hybrid microstrip integrated circuit power combined voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) operating at 35 GHz. Mutual injection locking is intentionally employed to obtain highly efficient power combining over a broad, spurious-free electronic tuning bandwidth. The performance of a dual Gunn diode, varactor tuned VCO assembled on a soft substrate is presented. This circuit is capable of producing a Ka-band output power of at least 1/2 watt with state-of-the-art InP Gunn diodes.

articleTitle: Generation of high power optical signals for 10–100 GHz optical transmission
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new technique has been developed for generation of high power optical signals in the 10–100 GHz frequency range using a single frequency modulated semiconductor laser and an interferometer. This technique offers a practical method for microwave carrier frequency optical communications and for distribution of microwave frequency local oscillator signals.

articleTitle: Simultaneous triple cascade operation of optically pumped submillimeter lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An optically pumped HCOOH laser has been operated simultaneously on three cascade rotational transitions. This leads to enhanced output power for all three transitions. The application of this mode of operation to interferometry is described.

articleTitle: Fundamental and second harmonic frequency generation from cusptron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Microwave radiation at fundamental and second harmonic cyclotron frequencies is generated from a cusptron oscillator with a smooth wall circuit. A low-energy, axis-rotating beam of 28–30 kV and 0.8–1.2 A interacts with a single RF-mode in a circular cavity by the negative mass instability. The independently excited modes are TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>‘s and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>‘s with radiation power of approximately 2.0 kW and an efficiency of 8.0%.

articleTitle: A frequency doubler for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a millimeter-wave. frequency doubler in corporating a novel mount structure whic combines suspend microstrip with fin-line and can be used in millimeter-wave integrated circut.

articleTitle: A 3mm heterodyne imaging array
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A heterodyne imaging array is under construction to tune the 95-115 GHz range with a 3×5 array. The mixers will use Schottky diodes operated at 20 K with integrated HEMT IF amplifiers. Image sideband rejection is done with a quasi-optical filter which terminates the image at 20 K. Polarization interleaving is used to minimize the array size on the sky.

articleTitle: Sidebands in free electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The problem of sideband growth in a free electron laser (FEL) is studied using canonical formalism. The exact unperturbed orbits, without sidebands, are obtained in action-angle variables for all particles. Integration of the linearized Vlasov equation with sidebands over the unperturbed orbits yields the sideband growth that includes both trapped and untrapped particles. It is found that the upper and lower sidebands that are symmetric about the FEL frequency have opposite growth rates, with equal magnitude. The stability of the upper or lower sidebands is determined by the sign of df<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>/dΩ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>, i.e., the relative population of oscillation quanta hΩ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>, Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> = bounce frequency around resonance.

articleTitle: Design, development and evaluation of a waveguide slot array at w-band
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves

authors.preferredName: S. K. L. V. Sai Prakash

abstract: A waveguide slot array with a required pattern is synthesized. One such array fabricated and tested to establish the design process and the fabrication techniques. Effect of tolerance in the length of the slot is critically discussed with reference to w-band frequencies.

articleTitle: High power CH3OH 70.5 μm laser to measure the absolute frequency of CO2 laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: To connect Cs standard frequency and CO2 laser, line, a CH3OH 70.5 urn laser with output power of more than 40 mW has been constructed. The performance of the laser and results of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> frequency measurement are presented.

articleTitle: Direct measurements of complex permittivity and permeability of magnetic materials
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Dispersive Fourier transform spectrometric technique was applied to a polarizing two beam interferometer to measure the complex magnetic permeability. The specimen was placed at the center of a Bitter solenoid high intensity magnet to seperate out complex magnetic permeability from combined dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability information. experimentally. The induced ferrimagnetic resonance moves to a higher frequency as the applied external magnetic field intensity values were increased to 100,000 Gauss. This reliable technique can now be used routinely: for the measurement of complex dielectric permittivity and complex magnetic permeability of cubic and hexagonal ferrite materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of periodically-illuminated optically controlled CPW phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The characteristics of a periodically-illuminated CPW phase shifter is investigated by the spectral domain approach combined with the cascaded transmission line equivalent circuit. It is found that the phase shifter characteristics can be improved by the use of periodic illumination instead of uniform illumination.

articleTitle: High-power te11 and tm11 circular polarizers in oversized waveguide at 70 ghz
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Elliptic deformation of oversized, smooth-wall circular waveguide can produce arbitrary elliptical or circular polarization from a linearly polarized TE11 or TM11 mode, used as intermediates between TE01 and HE11 in electron cyclotron heating (ECH) of magnetically confined thermonuclear fusion plasmas with high-power gyrotrons. Mode coupling in overmoded elliptically distorted circular waveguide has been studied theoretically and experimentally in order to optimize TE11 (and TM11) polarizers (I.D. = 27.79 mm) for use in the 1 MW/70 GHz ECH system on the Garching Stellarator W VII-AS. Accurate differential phase characteristics and very low levels of spurious modes have been achieved.

articleTitle: A ferrite sphere Y-junction waveguide circulator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel 4-mm waveguide circulator with a ferrite sphere is presented. The operation modes and frequency splits of the circulator are also discussed, and agreement between the predicted center frequencies and experiment values is obtained.

articleTitle: FEL-klystron for prebunched ka-band emission
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Preliminary analytical work has been performed on a low order prebunched FEL interaction, which exploits the narrow micropulse width of the beam produced by a linac compared to the wavelength of the generated wave. If the electrons are resonant with the FEL beat wave, then short electron micro-pulses will yield gain significantly higher than in the conventional FEL.

articleTitle: Scattering matrix analysis of inverted strip dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The microwave network theory has been used to analyze the inverted strip dielectric waveguides (ISG). The transverse resonance relations at the step discontinuity are expressed in the form of scattering matrices. The scattering matrices and their variation over a frequency range of 40–80 GHz have been obtained. The leakage from the structure has also been obtained in terms of strip width.

articleTitle: Neutron scattering from low-frequency excitations in a-sio2
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The temperature dependence of the inelastic neutron scattering intensity from vitreous silica has been studied between 50 and 300 K down to frequencies of 150 GHz. Above 500 GHz one finds essentially harmonic behaviour. The anharmonic behaviour at low frequencies can be described in a relaxational model using parameters determined from mechanical measurements. From their dynamic structure factor, the relaxations are coupled rotational jumps of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> tetrahedra. The jump width of the atoms in these relaxations is shown to be smaller than 0.8 Å. The results support the hypothesis of a common origin of the low temperatures glass anomalies.
