articleTitle: Initial operation of a high-power whispering-gallery-mode gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Varian has begun the development of a high-power gyrotron based on a whispering-gallery-mode interaction circuit. The first experimental tube has been designed to generate pulsed output powers up to 1 MW at a frequency of 140 GHz. The tube was also designed for CW operation at power levels of several hundred kilowatts. The overall design of the tube is discussed. Fabrication of the tube is hearing completion and initial tests on the tube will be carried out in the near future.

articleTitle: Design considerations for a sheet beam electron gun for the quasi-optical gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The quasi-optical gyrotron is a possible rf source for electron cyclotron resonances heating of large fusion reactors. To fully exploit its potential, a sheet beam electron gun should be utilized. A schematic and the parameters of the sheet beam gun are shown in Fig. 1. The gun shown is a magnetron injection gun modified for planar geometry. It actually produces a double sheet beam since up-down symmetry is assumed. In terms of the parameters of the beam in the gun, the gun parameters<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> are derived for the parameters shown by conservation of canonical momentum, adiabatic compression in the presence of a voltage drop V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>. The initial transverse energy comes from E × B motion in the voltage drop V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>. Limiting currents are determined by the current being a small fraction of the space charge limiting current, and also by the current being able to propagate through the interaction region. Both of these limiting currents turn out to be expressed in terms of a current per unit length rather than total current. Thus, by making the emitting region long enough, the gun is capable of putting out arbitrary current. The focusing electrode shapes can be determined by electrode synthesis, modified to a planar configuration.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> The remaining issue is of edge losses. We show that the electrode synthesis technique can be modified to shape edge electrodes in such a way as to minimize edge effects. Results for such an electron gun design will be shown. This work was supported by the Department of Energy.

articleTitle: Simulation for the operation characteristics of cusptron oscillators
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The operation characteristics of cusptron tubes are studied. We have evaluated the functional dependences of the saturation efficiencies on the beam energy, and on the ratio of the outer and inner radii of the tubes for three different cyclotron harmonics, i.e. N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 8, 10 and 12, and for both π mode and 2π mode operation.

articleTitle: Self-consistent nonlinear theory of the gyropeniotron amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A self-consistent three-dimensional nonlinear theory and a computer code were developed to investigate the potentially high efficiency operation of higher harmonic gyropeniotron amplifier. The results of simulation for cyclotron harmonic operation from 2nd to 8th harmonic with axis encircling electron orbits in the magnetron type circuit structure will be presented.

articleTitle: A new type of millimeter wave integrated directional couplers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new type of millimeter wave integrated directional couplers is presented. It is constructed by a series of E-plane fins and slots the lengthes of which are optimized. The design is based on the scattering matrix considering the effects of the thickness of fins and high order mode interactions at the step discontinuities. The calculated performance of two integrated couplers at Ka- and W-band are given.

articleTitle: Printed circuit antennas and fet detectors for millimeter-wave imaging
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Planar twin-dipole microstrip antennas with FET detectors have been constructed and found to provide antenna patterns suitable for millimeter-wave quasioptical applications. The circuits are suitable as individual elements of an imaging array.

articleTitle: Observation of millimeter wave ferromagnetic resonance in cubic and hexagonal ferrites
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Natural ferromagnetic resonance (in the absence of an externally applied DC magnetic field) has been observed at 240 GHz in a powdered magnetoplumbite suspended in a thin layer of paint. “Induced” ferromagnetic resonance has been observed at many millimeter wave frequencies in the presence of an externally applied magnetic field according to the rule: f = γ H.

articleTitle: New large offset fir laser lines from cd3oh and assignments in the c-o stretch
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The various isotopic species of methanol are responsible for more than 40% of all the known far infrared (FIR) laser lines [1]. More than 150 CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser lines have been assigned, due to both an easier interpretation of the coincidences between CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pump lines and absorptions, and to the availability of massive systematic assignment work for the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH spectrum[2]. The number of assigned FIR laser lines is much smaller for CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH, to which the present contribution is devoted. Our experimental apparatus consists, basically, of a waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser with a tunability of 300 MHz [3], and two FIR laser cavities. By means of this apparatus we had already observed 108 new CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH FIR laser lines [4].

articleTitle: High-temperature millimeter-wave dielectric measurements by free-space techniques
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Experimental measurement techniques have been developed for utilizing spot-focusing and collimating lens antennas to determine the millimeter-wave dielectric properties of planar samples over the frequency range 30–140 GHz at temperatures up to 1600°C. The method is suitable for studying the average bulk-sample dielectric properties as well as inhomogeneities on the dimensional scale of a wavelength. Other significant advantages of the method include: thermal isolation of the sample from the measurement apparatus, minimum sample preparation requirements, and convenience for screening a large number of samples in relatively short time periods. The measurement apparatus has been used to study a wide variety of materials, which has led to successful models for explaining the observed temperature dependence of the dielectric properties of polycrystalline ceramics.

articleTitle: Moist air attenuation at 96 GHz over a 21 km line-of-sight path
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Propagation experiments at 96.1 GHz over a 21.4 km line-of-sight path were conducted to investigate attenuation characteristics due to atmospheric water vapor in moist air. Temperature dependent attenuation rates were found to be in good agreement with a millimeter-wave propagation model (MPM) for an absolute humidity range from 3 to 21 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and a temperature range from 4 to 32°C.

articleTitle: Calculation of non-stationary effects in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A time-dependent slow-time-scale theory is developed for the analysis of high power, pulsed gyrotrons driven by external RF sources. Phase-locking of a gyrotron by direct injection of radiation into the cavity and by beam premodulation via a bunching cavity is investigated. Calculations are carried out to simulate the operation of a 35 GHz high voltage gyrotron.

articleTitle: Nonlinear beam-wave interaction in a harmonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Applying a ballistic method, an analysis of the nonlinear beam-wave interaction in a harmonic gyrotron is presented. A set of general equations with three normalized parameters is derived. The expressions of the total efficiency and the output power of the device for TEn1 mode are also given.

articleTitle: Far infrared characterization of semiconductor microstructures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Intricate semiconductor microstructures require varied methods to examine their properties. Far infrared (FIR) spectroscopy (10–400 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) is contactless and nondestructive. articleTitle: Synthesis of bandpass grid filter for linear polarized millimeter wave
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A method based on equivalent circuit and transmission line model is proposed to design narrow bandpass grid filters in short MM-wave. Several bandpass filters with 2,3 or 4 element inductive wire grids in the 70 GHz region have been designed with Butterworth or Chebyshev characteristic for linear polarized wave. The agreement between measurement and theory proves the rationality of our theory.

articleTitle: The 150 GHz gyrotron experiment at the kernforschungszentrum karlsruhe
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent experimental results of the 150 GHz Gyrotron at KfK will be presented. The highest power reached in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf>–mode so far is 120 kw at 1 ms pulse length. A brief description of the diagnostic methods (frequency measurement, calorimeter, mode analyser etc.) as well as a comparison with theoretical calculations will be given.

articleTitle: Crosstie overlay slow-wave structure for broadband traveling-wave type electro-optical modulator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper proposes a new crosstie overlay slow-wave structure for a traveling-wave electro-optical modulator. This structure can be designed to satisfy the phase velocity and impedance matching conditions simultaneously over a broad spectral bandwidth. This idea can be applied to a number of electrode structures for broadband traveling-wave optical modulators.

articleTitle: Results of a large orbit, high harmonic gyro-twt amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 16.2 GHz large orbit Gyro-TWT amplifier has been operated at the eighth cyclotron harmonic with a small signal gain of 10 dB, an interaction bandwidth of 4.3%, and a saturated power transfer from the electron beam to the wave of 0.5 kW. Most importantly, the experimental results are in good agreement with the predictions of the analytic dispersion relationship for the interaction (1), permitting the design of scaled, high performance tubes.

articleTitle: Propagation studies in the region of the oxygen absorption band in an urban environment
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Experimental results obtained from a propagation study carried out on a 55GHz mobile radio link in Central London are presented. Results indicate that frequencies in this region are a viable proposition for a potential mobile radio system from the propagation point of view. The bandwidth in the multipath environment appears to be adequate and polarisation diversity is also a possibility.

articleTitle: A far infrared study of shallow acceptors in gaas/algaas quantum wells
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Far infrared transmission has been used to study beryllium acceptors doped in the center of GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells and bulk GaAs. From the infrared measurements a binding energy of 28.5meV was inferred, in agreement with photoluminescence measurements. The effects of confinement are evident in shifts to progressively higher frequencies of the dominant transitions as the well width is decreased from 200Å to 100Å. The magnetic field dependence of the observed transitions has been investigated between 0 and 9.0T at temperatures between 4.2 and 30K for the bulk sample and 200Å well width sample. The shifts of the transitions with magnetic field are much smaller than predicted by recent calculations for confined acceptors.

articleTitle: Properties of evaporated ge thin-films for warm carrier devices
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recently, there has been growing interest in thin-film antenna-coupled infrared laser detectors. In the thin-film infrared laser detectors, the warm carrier devices have been fabricated using the single crystal Ge wafer<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. But if these devices could be fabricated by using Ge thin-films deposited on insulating substrates, it would be attractive for flexibility of fabrication of the device structure. The responsivity of these devices, on the other hand, is proportional to the carrier mobility of semiconductor films<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>. Therefore, semiconducting-films with large carrier mobility are necessary instead of the single crystal Ge wafer.

articleTitle: Backward-wave interaction using step periodic structures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Periodicities introduced into hollow waveguides with step and turn symmetry are shown to have characteristics useful for backward-wave interaction in microwave electron tubes. Using Floquet's theorem, it is shown that the modes of a hollow waveguide can be shifted in phase over one period of the structure. Interaction with the shifted backward-wave mode is then possible over a range of frequencies. A gyrotron backward-wave oscillator is particularly suited to this structure; the interaction could be magnetically tuned over a range of frequencies, while a low phase constant is maintained. A solid waveguide has the added advantages of being easily built for high frequencies and rugged for higher temperatures.

articleTitle: A study of the efficiencies of high harmonic gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We study, by particle simulation, the conversion efficiency of a large orbit gyrotron. The dependence of the saturation efficiency of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N1</inf> mode on the harmonic number N = 2-16 and beam energy γo are determined.

articleTitle: A comparison of line-of-sight transmissions at millimetre, infrared and optical wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A comparison has been made of line-of-sight propagation over a 500 m path at millimetre, infrared and optical wavelengths, under a wide variety of meteorological conditions. The results indicate that, for climates prone to conditions of fog, the millimetric region of the electromagnetic spectrum provides a more effective and reliable means of communication.

articleTitle: Far infrared dielectric loss and low frequency Raman scattering in chalcogenide glasses
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Important information about the nature of the ubiquitous low frequency Raman peak (“Bose peak”), which is commonly observed in network glasses, can be obtained from a detailed comparison of the Raman Scattering and the far infrared dielectric loss. New dielectric loss data for vitreous As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> will be presented and interpreted in terms of a unified model for low frequency modes in this glass.

articleTitle: Far infrared photoconductivity experiments on the si donor in gaas
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The far infrared photoconductivity of Si doped GaAs has been studied using an optically pumped FIR laser working in the 10-150 cm range. At temperatures between H and 10 K in magnetic fields up to 12 T an almost complete set of transitions from the shallow (Si) donor groundstate to the excited hydrogenic levels (n = 2,3,4) is observed. The obtained field dependence of the energy levels is in good agreement with theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Selectable-finesse fabry-perot interferometer for the frequency measurements of millimeter and submillimeter waves
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A scanning Fabry-Perot interferometer with selectable reflection-finesse is proposed for wide range operation over millimeter and submillimeter waves. The stripe directions of the two striped polarizing reflectors are made slightly different and the reflectance is varied according to the relative angle of two stripe directions. The optimization of reflection-finesse for frequency measurements is achieved by adjusting the relative angle. The experimental results show the possibility of selecting reflection-finesse over wide frequency range without exchanging reflectors.

articleTitle: Modulation of an intense beam by an external microwave source in the non-linear regime — theory and simulation
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A time dependent, fully electromagnetic particle code is used to simulate the current modulation in an intense relativistic electron beam (IREB) by an external rf source in the nonlinear regime. It is shown that non-linear effects, responsible for the high modulation levels seen in the experiments(1,2), may be explained via simple models and the non-linear propagation of fast and slow space charge waves. Qualitative and quantitative agreement between the theory and simulations is obtained.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave phase shifters based on microwave-induced birefringence
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Millimeter wave phase shifters based on microwave-induced birefringence in artificial Kerr media have been demonstrated. Full-wave phase shifts produced by alignment of rod-shaped particles in a liquid suspension make possible the development of millimeter wave analogs of nonlinear optical devices.

articleTitle: Ballistic model of free electron laser interactions
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The equation of motion of relativistic electrons moving in both helical wiggler fields and propagating waves of unspecified and unknown polarization is solved under small signal conditions. The general solution reveals that five different interactions are possible, classified as “synchronous” and “resonant”. These five interactions can become degenerate when the applied axial DC magnetic field is small or zero, and when its value is close to the critical value at which the DC electron orbits become unstable. The properties of these interactions are summarized. Because of the generalized field of the wave, the approach is valid for self-fields and the superposition of TE and TM modes as well.

articleTitle: Vibrational densities of states for glassy se-ge alloys by neutron scattering
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Densities of states for vibrational excitations in Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1–x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> glasses with 0≤x≤0.33 have been determined by neutron scattering methods. The low-energy portions of the spectra exhibit floppy modes which rapidly diminish in number with Ge addition. The results are discussed in terms of rigidity percolation, and correspondence with other experimental properties.

articleTitle: Development of high efficiency W-band microstrip circuit doublers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using packaged GaAs varactor diodes, high efficiency doubler circuits have been developed at W-band. Microstrip circuits are used to match the input and output impedances presented by the diode. A conversion loss of 8 to 10 dB was measured from 9 0 to 93 GHz. For narrowband, circuits can be tuned to work with a conversion loss of less than 6.5 dB. These doubler circuits are suitable for W-band integrated circuit receivers and trans-receivers in which a stable local oscillator power is a problem. Use of microstrip drastically reduces the fabrication cost, in addition to size and weight.

articleTitle: On the high resolution far infrared spectroscopy of c-13 methanol: b-type r-branches in the torsional ground state
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The high-resolution FTFIR spectrum of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH has been studied from 25-350 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Assignments of b-type R-branches in the torsional ground state have yielded phenomenological expansion parameters for the torsion-rotation energy levels. An interesting localized perturbation in the (nτK)=(019) state is discussed.

articleTitle: Sideband instability in a free electron laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A two-dimensional, axisymmetric, time-dependent simulation code is used to examine the growth of sideband instabilities in a free electron laser amplifier. We examine the exponential growth and the nonlinear regimes. It is found that in a tapered wiggler, after an initial period of rapid increase in amplitude, the growth of sideband modes virtually ceases, saturating at a level substantially below that of the main signal.

articleTitle: A new design method of H-plane waveguide circulator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new method to design the partial height ferrite posts of H-plane waveguide circulator for given frequencies is presented. Agreement between calculated design results and experiment values in [1] and our MMW waveguide circulators are obtained.

articleTitle: Some progress in techniques of MMW and sub MMW detection
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An accurate laser frequency measurement system using SMM harmonic mixing technique is presented. A novel power-meter with a high sensitivity 50–100μV/μW for 26.5–170GHZ and for 50μW-1.2W (cw)/100W (pulse) power is described. Besides, the improvement of the heterodyne receiving system for plasma diagnosis is introduced.

articleTitle: Ka band digitally addressed attenuator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A OdBm Ka Band Waveguide PIN diode stepped attenuator giving up to 45dB of attenuation is described. The attenuator is digitally addressed in steps of 0.5dB whilst maintaining a return loss better than 20dB at one port over a 1 GHz band, Details of the drive circuit and switching characteristics are presented and system applications are discussed briefly.

articleTitle: A novel high power coherent semiconductor fir source
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The mode structure of p-Ge far infrared lasers with and without mirrors is investigated. Without external mirrors a multimode spectrum is observed and quantitatively explained in terms of waveguidelike modes. An external resonator drastically reduces the number of oscillating modes. For the first time, oscillation on a single longitudinal mode is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of millimeter-wave fin-line bandpass filters
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel systematic program for CAD of millimeter-wave fin-line bandpass filters has been developed. Owimg to the application of a simple and efficient mathematical model for fin-line discontinuities, considerably more CPU time can be saved during the optimization circles.

articleTitle: Summary of submillimeter (terahertz) receiver technology conference at lake arrowhead
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The submillimeter wavelength region spanning the octave from 1 mm to 0.1 mm (300 to 3000 GHz) is one of the last major windows in the electromagnetic spectrum to be explored. The primary application for submillimeter wave technology has been basic scientific research including astrophysics, atmospheric physics, plasma diagnostics, and laboratory spectroscopy. More recently this spectral range is being considered for space-based radar and communications systems to combine the frequency resolution and agility available in the microwave regime with the high spatial resolution with modest apertures typical of optical technology. Since the earth's atmosphere is opaque except in a few discrete windows, throughout the submillimeter, much of the technology development is being directed toward space qualifiable components and sponsored by NASA or DOD.

articleTitle: High performance MM-wave balanced mixers for ka-band down-converters
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The design and development of mm-wave finline and crossbar suspended stripline balanced mixer for Ka-Band downconverters is described. A convertion loss of 5.9±0.6dB over the frequency band 32 to 36 GHz has been achieved in a crossbar stripline structure, and 6.5±0.7dB over the frequency band 26,5 to 40 GHz in a fin-line with suspended stripline structure.

articleTitle: Image guide couplers used in millimeter wave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The dispersion and coupling characteristics of the coupled image guides are studied by using the odd-even mode principle and effective dielectric constant method. The practical design of the image quide directional couplers is presented. The experiments of 3-dB and 10-dB couplers in ka band show several good features which are very useful to millimeter wave integrated circuits with flat coupling, easy design and fabrication, mechanical stability and low losses.

articleTitle: The performance of schottky diodes as far-infrared modulators
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We analyze the performance as a terahertz-frequency, reflective modulator of a small-area Schottky diode mounted in a corner-cube antenna. The analysis includes the effects of carrier inertia and dielectric relaxation (1), and of the vanishing of the depletion region above the flat-band potential, (2,3). Our baseline calculation refers to a 1.4 μm diameter diode operated at a carrier frequency of 2.52 THz and a modulation frequency of 8 GHz, as was used in our experiments (4,5). Our conclusions are: A) For all realistic diode parameters, the phase modulation completely dominates the amplitude modulation. B) Performance is degraded well below the plasma frequency in the undepleted epilayer due to the presence of a second resonance, caused by the interaction of the barrier capacitance and the effective inductance due to carrier inertia, C) The effects of varying the antenna impedance, temperature, diode substrate size, and Schottky barrier height over realistic ranges are small. D) An improvement in single-sideband conversion efficiency of approximately 20 db may be obtained by increasing the epilayer doping and simultaneously reducing the diode radius. Agreement between the calculated and measured conversion efficiencies at 2.52 THz is very good.

articleTitle: A 120–240 GHz step tunable megawatt gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A pulsed (3μsec) gyrotron oscillator which can be scaled to cw operation has generated high output powers at frequencies between 126 and 243 GHz. Peak powers of 645 kW and total efficiencies of 28% were measured. By varying the cavity magnetic field, step tuning through a sequence of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m,p,1</inf> modes with p = 2,3 and 4 was observed. The highest order mode observed was the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22,4,1</inf> at 243 GHz, which corresponds to a cavity diameter of 12 free space wavelengths. An output power of 470 kW was measured in this mode at 80 kV and 35 A.

articleTitle: Broad band mm TWT amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: 100 watts of CW output power and 20% minimum efficiency have been obtained from an octave bandwidth traveling wave tube at frequencies up to 40 GHz. The tube employs periodic permanent magnet focusing, a unique brazed-notched rod circuit technology, a Pierce gun, a two-stage depressed collector, and WRD-180 input/output waveguides. Design highlights and performance data are presented.

articleTitle: Gyrotron scattering from non-thermal fluctuations in the tara tandem mirror
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 137 GHz, ∼0.4 kW, 75 ms pulsed gyrotron has been used for collective Thomson scattering in the Tara Tandem Mirror plug cell at MIT [1]. Scattering from ion cyclotron waves during ion cyclotron resonance frequency (ICRF) heating, ion Bernstein wave harmonics, and plasma fluctuations possibly due to microinstabilities have been observed. The observed harmonic nature of the ion Bernstein waves may be due to an enhanced ion thermal frequency spectrum in an ICRF heated plasma.

articleTitle: An infrared interferometer/polarimeter on the compact ignition tokamak
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The results of a feasibility study of a two-dimensional infrared interferometer/polarimeter system for measurements of electron density and plasma current profiles in the Compact Ignition Tokamak (CIT) are presented. Both horizontal and vertical systems utilize c-w CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers at a wave-length of 10.6 μm. The choice of this wavelength results mainly from a trade-off, being sufficiently short to limit the angle of beam refraction by plasma density gradients to an acceptable value, yet sufficiently long to obtain adequate sensitivity for the measurements. A two-wavelength scheme is used to correct the measuring errors caused by mechanical vibrations of the mirrors. Because of the large currents and particle densities in CIT, large Faraday rotation and Voigt effects are expected at long wavelengths. In order to ensure the successful design of the system, the propagation of the infrared waves in CIT plasmas is being investigated. An algorithm for the solution of the wave equation is developed and is used to determine the polarization evolution on the Poincare sphere. Computer codes are utilized to calculate the ellipticity ∊ and the Faraday rotation angle of the vibrational ellipse of the polarization, θ. For a parabolic density distribution with CIT plasma parameters, the maximum 9 is approximately 1.54°, the maximum ∊ is 4.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> (Fig. 1), and the maximum phase shift due to electron density φ is approximately 1.85 fringes. In Table 1, the values of θ, ∊, and φ at several wavelengths are summarized for both CIT and the presently operating Tokamak Fusion Test Reactor (TFTR). As expected, the effect of the ellipticity of the polarization is not negligible even at a wavelength of 70 μm. In an earlier paper (1), it was shown that both the amplitude and the phase of the detector signals depend strongly on the ellipticity of the polarization.

articleTitle: Non reciprocal single mode conversion in five-layer magnetooptical waveguides
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Five-layer wave-guiding structures are of great interest in magnetooptical for their use in the making of single-mode devices. In this work, non reciprocal single-mode conversion TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in a five–layer magnetooptical waveguide using infrared light (1.51μm) has been studied.

articleTitle: Preliminary design of a 280 ghz, 1 mw cw gyrotron oscillator
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In order to address auxiliary heating requirements for the Compact Ignition Torus and the Experimental Test Reactor, Varian has conducted a preliminary design study to determine the potential for gyrotrons as rf sources for electron cyclotron heating. The U.S. Department of Energy is seeking devices capable of producing rf at 280 GHz with power levels between 1 and 2 MW continuous-wave (CW). The source must be step-tunable in frequency by 30% and capable of single-mode operation. Varian is currently developing a 1 MW CW gyrotron at 140 GHz, and much of the technology obtained in that program will be directly applicable to development of a 280 GHz source.

articleTitle: Far-infrared conductivity of yba2Cu3O7–y
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We review experimental data on the optical conductivity of YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7–y</inf> Kramers-Kronig analysis shows that in the mid infrared range the optical conductivity is typical of perovskites with a rich phonon structure in the oxygen bond stretching and bending region. In the far infrared a depression of conductivity sets in below the superconducting transition temperature that we associate with the presence of a superconducting energy gap. In all the samples we have looked at there is residual conductivity in the gap.

articleTitle: On interpretation of airborne radiometric measurements at 30 and 90 GHz
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This work refers to the problem of interpreting and explaining measured data. The problem indicated is general but the presentation will be limited to comprise only some attempts related to airborne radiometer measurements at 31 and 93 GHz. Calculations of the information content of measured data will be given. The method used is essentially based on communication theory concepts.

articleTitle: The theoretical properties of higher mode cylindrical dielectric resonators for millimetre wave monolithic circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This work extends our previous studies of square cuboid dielectric resonators to the cylindrical pill types. The microstrip substrates considered are gallium arsenide and a polyimide, and calculations have been undertaken for all the resonant modes. Particular attention is given to the much used high Q TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">016</inf> mode, and the higher Q HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">126</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01(1+δ)</inf> modes that we have used in several applications. The frequencies of the other TE, TM, EH and HE modes have been calculated to determine the resonator aspect ratio that minimises mode interference. Data presented include the effect of resonator permittivity, substrate thickness and permittivity, and the effect of circuit package. Experimental data are discussed briefly.

articleTitle: Submillimeter laser scattering from a tokamak plasma
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Submillimeter laser scattering using an optically pumped HCOOH laser has been used to study low frequency MHD phenomena in a smalll tokamak plasma. The same scattering system is being applied to an Alfven wave heating experiment.

articleTitle: The far infrared dielectric properties of conducting polymers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Dielectric properties of polypyrrole films in the FIR, 10–200 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, are investigated. Control of these properties, in particular the conductivity, is achieved by changing the level of doping through oxidation-reduction during synthesis of the polymer. The dielectric constants of the conducting polymer films studied were found to exhibit a large frequency dependence in this spectral region.

articleTitle: Efficiency of CH2F2 laser lines at 184 and 214 micron operating with cascade transitions
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The previously reported efficient FIR lines in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at 184 and 214 microns have been shown to operate with cascade transitions. The resultant efficiency of these lines will be discussed. An experimental and theoretical discussion will be presented.

articleTitle: Anisotropic reflectivity of black phosphorus in the far-infrared region
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Black phosphorus, which is the most stable allotropic modification of phosphorus, is a semiconductor with a narrow-band gap of 0.3 eV [1]. The crystal is composed of puckered layers of atoms and belongs to an orthorhombic crystal structure (D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2h</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1e</sup>). The structure of the puckered layer is schematically shown in Fig. la with a cartesian coordinate. According to its crystal symmetry, two infrared active phonon modes, i.e. B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1u</inf> and B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3u</inf> modes, are predicted to exist at the F point of the Brillouin zone [2]. Although black phosphorus possesses no permanent dipole moment because four atoms in the primitive unit cell are the same, it has been pointed out by a theoretical work [2] that an effective dipole moment will be induced by the atomic displacement according to each infrared active mode. The induced dipole moment due to the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3u</inf> mode is directed along the z-axis of the crystal and that due to the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1u</inf> mode along the x-axis. The lattice vibration according to the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1u</inf> mode is drawn in Fig. 1b. The B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3u</inf> phonon mode was observed at 470 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> by infrared absorption [3, 4] and reflection measurements [5] and the direction of its induced dipole moment was confirmed to lie in the direction of the z-axis of the crystal. Up to now, on the other hand, a quantitative measurement on the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1u</inf> mode has not been done. Sugai and Shirotani [53 made first a reflection measurement at the room temperature in the far-infrared region and observed a sharp peak which was assigned to the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1u</inf> phonon mode. However, a quantitative analysis was not given because of the difficulty of a precise measurement of the reflectivity on a small solid specimen in this region.

articleTitle: Optimized efficiency of the ten1 interaction with fast axis-rotating electron beams
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A nonlinear analysis of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n1</inf> interaction with a fast axis-rotating electron beam is performed to determine the efficiencies of the interaction for a wide range of parameters. In this analysis a single nonlinear third-order differential equation is derived for describing the temporal evolution of the wave field for the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n1</inf> interaction of a fast axis-rotating beam in a waveguide of cylindrical geometry, operated in the amplifier mode. The equation may be solved numerically for the wave field amplitude as a function of time over its entire range. From knowledge of the wave field amplitude at saturation, the efficiency may be directly calculated. The efficiency of the interaction is then optimized as a function of wave frequency.

articleTitle: Phonon, plasmon and gap behavior in high-temperature copper oxide superconductors
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Infrared spectroscopy of conventional superconductors shows Drude electronic behavior above T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, gap behavior below T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, and almost no phonons because of screening. In contrast, our spectra (50–600 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) of the rare earth barium copper oxides R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> B a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3–x</inf> C u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> (R =Y, Gd, Tm; x= 1, 1.5) show few carriers and strong phonon modes. The spectra yield 2Δ/kT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> ≥ 3.6 and suggest enhanced plasmon-phonon interaction near the gap which may be important for high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> superconductivity (1–4).

articleTitle: Theory of 1attice excitations in predicted alkali halide superlattice
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Superlattices of alkali halides might have novel absorption properties if they could be made. In particular extremely low frequency absorption would be expected, due to zone-folding of the dispersion curves, especially if the superlattice lacked inversion symmetry whereby all optic modes are potentially active. It is possible to reasonably explore such superlattices theoretically in view of the success of the ab initio Gordon-Kim theory (1,2) in describing structural and thermal properties of known closed-shell ionic materials. In that theory the energy is expressed in terms of two-body central forces including long range ionic Coulomb forces. The perturbation theory treatment for the dielectric properties in terms of cubic and quartic anharmonic coefficients has been worked out (3), and, combined with the Gordon-Kim theory, can be used to obtain ab initio theoretical predictions of dielectric properties of ionic materials.

articleTitle: Recent advances in tunable Raman fir lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As new gain media are investigated and new optical pumping conditions are employed, the spectral coverage produced by Raman FIR lasers continues to expand. Concommitant efforts to improve the theoretical modeling are improving our understanding of the laser and contributing to the optimization of its performance.

articleTitle: Parametric analysis for a millimeter wave low noise high electron mobility transistor
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper presents parametric analysis for low noise High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) devices suitable for mm-wave radar, satellite communication and radiometric applications. Preliminary computations reveal that pseudomorphic HEMT devices using InGaAs/GaAs heterojunction structures offer significant improvements in power added efficiency, noise figure, gain, reliability, and input power requirements compared to standard HEMT's. A Pseudomorphic HEMT device is capable of providing a room temperature noise figure of 3.5dB and small signal gain of 8dB at 95 GHz, approximately.

articleTitle: Higher order modes and crystallographic axis angular dependence of propagation in anisotropic pbn using a spectral matrix method
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 4×4 field matrix method for layered structures is employed to numerically calculate the propagation constant γ for coupled microstrip on a highly anisotropic material, Pyrolitic boron nitride (PBN). This new technique is very versatile, and allows the determination of γ for arbitrary permittivity, principle axis crystallographic orientation θ. Even and odd mode propagation constants are found for θ = 0°, 45°, and 90°. The approach is fully dynamic, yielding the dispersion characteristics of each of the modes studied. Numerical data is provided in the microwave and millimeter wave regions.

articleTitle: An experimental investigation of energy transfer in optically pumped fir lasers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We conducted a time-resolved double resonance study of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F to explore the rotational and vibrational energy transfer processes in this optically pumped far infrared (OPFIR) laser. The use of a Q-switched CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser and sensitive, tunable millimeter and submillimeter (mm/submm) techniques allowed us to probe not only the gain profile of the laser transition, but also many other states that are collisionally coupled and play important roles in the energy transfer process (1,2).

articleTitle: Far infrared detection without preamplifiers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An injection pulse phenomenon<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup> which can be used to detect infrared (IR) radiation without the use of preamplifiers at 4.2K is described and analyzed.

articleTitle: The third cyclotron harmonic gyromonotron with a ridged waveguide
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Eigenvalues and fields of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf> modes in a ridged waveguide are derived in this paper. The field distribution of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> indicates the difficulty of peniotron's realization in the waveguide. After comparing the fields of TE10 and TE30 with that of TE10 and TE30 rectangular waveguide modes, nonlinear calculations have been carried out on models of large-orbit gyrotron oscillators with a ridged resonator or a rectangular one. It has been studied that the transverse fields affect the efficiency of the gyrotron at the fundamental or the third cyclotron harmonic. The computational results show the gyrotron oscillator at the third cyclotron harmonic and using TE301 in the ridged waveguide has 51% high efficiency.

articleTitle: Coupling between Gaussian and guided mode at the input and output of oversized circular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The coupling between a gaussian TEMOO mode with HE modes for dielectric waveguides is analytically studied. An optimization method allows us to know how HE11 or TE11 modes create gaussian TEMNM modes at the ouput of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Analysis of dynamically generated slow-wave structures in the magneto-orotron free-electron laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Radiation associated with the dynamically generated slow-wave structures in the magnetoorotron free-electron laser (a hybrid of the orotron and the uniform magnetic field free-electron lasers) is analyzed semielassically. This analysis is aimed at eventually giving a complete description of the device, which is capable of generating radiation in the far-infrared/microwave spectral region.

articleTitle: Fir results in [pd (-chnx) 2br] br2
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The FIR transmission spectrum of [Pd(-chnx)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Br] Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was studied in magnetic fields up to 7 T and at temperatures below 2.5 K. With the magnetic field oriented perpendicular to the c-axis, several peaks were observed. The origin of these is not yet well understood.

articleTitle: Tuning behavior of a ch3f amplified spontaneous emission laser
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using a single mode tuneable CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser to pump the Q(12) transition in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> F and a heterodyne receiver to make frequency measurements on the resulting FIR radiation, we have documented the near resonance tuning behavoir of this FIR Raman transition as the pump laser is tuned. Nonlinear frequency tuning of FIR emission is observed due to inhomogeneous (K level) broadening of the Raman transition.

articleTitle: Broadband millimeter wave generation with folded waveguide circuit
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using a serpentine waveguide as an interaction circuit, amplification over an instantaneous band from 40 to 54 GHz has been achieved in a low-gain PPM focused TWT. Mid-band power output was more than 300 W with basic efficiency of over 7 percent. Such circuits are more rugged than helices, and are broader band and much easier to manufacture than coupled-cavity circuits.

articleTitle: On the high resolution infrared spectroscopy of the c-0 stretch band of 13CH3OH: Phenomenological parameters for the a-species in the torsional ground state
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Results of extensive analysis of the high resolution Fourier transform spectrum of the C-O stretch band of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH are presented for the A torsional symmetry species in the n=0 torsional ground state, in terms of phenomenological state-dependent parameters. FIR laser assignments associated with (nτK)=(019) states are also discussed.

articleTitle: High Harmonic Emission from Slotted rectangular gyrotron oscillators
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Start oscillation conditions are considered for rectangular slotted gyrotron cavities. It is found that the addition of slots to a cavity lowers the required beam power for oscillation at high harmonics and can lead to a decrease of the start oscillation beam power as the harmonic number is increased. Previous gyrotron cavity designs have consistently shown the start oscillation beam power increasing with harmonic number. Slotted devices thus appear potentially attractive as a means of achieving millimeter wave emission.

articleTitle: The nrl quasi-optical gyrotron experiment
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The design of a 110 GHz, 100 kw gyrotron is presented. The setup is very flexible, allowing for the easy study of many different resonator configurations. Resonant cavities with different longitudinal mode spacing (7% ≥ Δf/f ≥ 0.5%) will be tested, as well as cavities having different electromagnetic radiation waist lengths (r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> = 0.6,1.2 cm). This experiment has been assembled and data is currently being collected.

articleTitle: Loss and mode characteristics of oversized waveguides and resonators
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Oversized waveguides and resonators offer advantageous solutions of the waveguiding and circuit problems at millimeter-wave frequencies. They have low losses and high Q factors in comparison with rectangular waveguides of standard sizes and with miniaturized structures, such as microstrip and fin line. Also, manufacturing of integrated circuits based on suitable types of oversized structures is inexpensive. The sizes which are in the magnitude of millimeters are relatively small and, if compared with the usual dimensions of antennas, practical. Miniaturized structures, in comparison with the required antenna dimensions, are only marginally practical.

articleTitle: A short-period wiggler millimeter-wave free electron laser for plasma heating and space-borne radar
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We will report on the status of a new mm-wave FEL research program based on short-period electromagnet wigglers and a low voltage (500 kV) sheet electron beam. Recent results of measurements and theoretical modeling will be discussed. Potential applications of this device include space-based radar and electron cyclotron heating of the magnetic fusion plasmas.

articleTitle: Air-to-air applications for millimeter-wave communications
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The performance of millimeter-wave (MMW) communications techniques for air-to-air applications is reviewed. The anti-jam (AJ) and low-probability-of intercept (LPI) performance of a communications system resulting from the attenuative characteristics of the atmosphere in the 50–60 GHz band are characterized. The objective of the communications system design is to avoid traditional AJ and LPI techniques such as spread-spectrum modulation and narrow-beam antennas, resulting in a simple system with a robust and secure communications capability.

articleTitle: Assignments of fir laser lines from non-co-stretch states of CH3OH
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Assignments are discussed for optically-pumped CH3OH FIR laser lines originating from transitions in other than pure C-0 stretch states. The assignments are confirmed by formation of closed combination loops of measured frequencies, or are supported by direct FTFIR spectral observations for refilling transitions.

articleTitle: Final design and initial operation of a high peak power x-band gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The feasibility of using gyroklystrons in linear collider applications is currently under investigation at the University of Maryland.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> We are constructing a four-cavity X-band tube which is predicted to achieve a peak power of 30–50 MW in 1–2 us pulses with an efficiency of 45% and a gain of 63 dB. This goal represents an increase in the state-of-the-art by three orders of magnitude in power<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is close to predicted collider requirements.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical gyrotron with arbitrary beam injection angle
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In quasi-optical gyrotrons <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1–4)</sup> the angle between the electron and radiation beams has considerable influences on gain, harmonic operation and efficiency. This paper investigates the effect on the gain mechanism. Two regimes of operation are identified. By choosing the parameters appropriately one can run the gyrotron in the high gain regime.

articleTitle: Depressed collectors for a large orbit gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An auxiliary magnetic cusp transforms rotational motion in the spent beam of a Large-Orbit Gyrotron into axial motion. Results regarding the interfacing of this cusp with a depressed collector region and the effects of the magnetic field profile together with collector geometry and potentials on energy sorting are discussed.

articleTitle: Peniotrons at mm-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper presents experimental results for traditional peniotron devices operating in the mm-wave frequency range, using a unique electron gun and a new technique to fabricate quadruple ridge waveguides. More than 300 W of amplified output power with 17-dB gain was measured with such a device at 45 GHz, and 750 W of output power was observed when operated as an oscillator.

articleTitle: Aperture efficiency of ltsa focal plane arrays for millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The aperture efficiency for elements in focal plane arrays, when used in multi-beam (imaging) systems has been estimated with a new method which makes use of measured data for both radiation patterns and absolute gain for the elements of the array. Data for LTSA arrays show that aperture efficiencies and element gains can be close to the upper bounds predicted by theory, at element spacings which are about twice the sampling limit spacing. Such arrays should be very useful for millimeter wave imaging and power combining.

articleTitle: Millimeterwave frequency extension radar warning receiver
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a ‘proof of concept’ millimeterwave Frequency Extension Receiver (F.X.R.) designed as an add-on to an existing microwave airborne system. The F.X.R. extends the frequency coverage from the existing microwave region to greater than 100 GHz using commutatively switched downconverters. A key feature of this receiver is the modular construction which allows it to be added on to many existing microwave receiver systems.

articleTitle: High-j infrared spectrum and far-infrared laser assignments in ch3oh
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: High-resolution Fourier transform spectra of CH3OH have been obtained in the high-J wings of the P and R branches of the C-O stretch band, to refine the molecular constants and to search for coincidences with CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser lines. Energy level expansion coefficients are reported describing branches in the n=0 and n=l torsional states. From the analysis, several IR-pump/FIR-laser transition systems have been assigned, and a number of previous assignments confirmed.

articleTitle: Precision millimeter and submillimeter wave measurements of material properties
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Dielectric measurement techniques developed over last twelve years are reviewed. Varieties of measurement techniques are necessary in order to cope with material problems such as absorption characteristics, size and thickness, shape and temperature and frequency coverage. Precision data are now required on absorption coefficient, refractive index, real and imaginary parts of dielectric permittivity and loss tangent for varieties of classes of materials over a wide frequency range for applications such as substrate, window and lens material, as dielectric waveguide, quarter wave plates, insulators and in integrated circuitry.

articleTitle: Molecular absorption intensity measurements in the millimeter wavelength region
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Techniques are discussed for measurement of molecular absorption intensity in the millimeter wavelength region with Fabry-Perot Interferometers. Comparison is made with other intensity measuring schemes. Included in the presentation are experimental and theoretical considerations of cavity characteristics, pressure effects, spectral line density, hydrogen bonding, measurement techniques and source stability.

articleTitle: 85 GHz te1,3 phase-locked gyroklystron oscillator experiment
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Phase-locked gyroklystron oscillators offer many advantages over conventional gyrotrons including better mode control resulting in higher efficiency operation, narrow band frequency tunability and the possibility of coherently combining many sources for ultra-high power applications. We are studying phase-locking of highly overmoded gyrotrons at moderate power levels (∼100 kw) in an 85 GHz two cavity TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,3</inf> gyroklystron oscillator configuration as shown in Figure 1. articleTitle: Experiments for an eighth harmonic cusptron tube
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have set up a cusptron device to compare the performance of π mode and 2π mode operation at 8th harmonic interaction. A concentric e-layer of of 30 Kev (γ=1.06) is produced for wave generation. For 2π mode operation, an 8-slotted waveguide with b/a = 22 is used, where b and a are the radii of the vane and the inner wall of the waveguide respectively. In order to achieve same output frequency for comparison, a 16-slotted waveguide with b/a =1.23 is used for π mode operation. The arrangement of the set up will be described. The preliminary results of the experiments will also be presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave monolithic transceivers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A significant program Is currently underway 1n the United States to Investigate, develop, and produce a variety of GaAs analog circuits for use 1n microwave and millimeter wave sensors and systems. This represents a “new wave” of RF technology which promises to significantly change system engineering thinking relative to RF Architectures. At millimeter wave frequencies, we look forward to a relatively high level of critical component integration based on MESFET and HEMT device Implementations. These designs will spawn more compact RF front ends with colocated antenna/transceiver functions and innovative packaging concepts which will survive and function 1n a typical military operational environment which includes challenging temperature, shock, and special handling requirements.

articleTitle: The status of millimeter wave hybrid integrated-circuit balanced mixers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The development of millimeter wave hybrid integrated circuit balanced mixers using two-terminal devices has been considered nearly mature. In this paper, the present state of this technology is reviewed. Advantages and disadvantages of existing mixer configurations are discussed along with their measured performances. Some new configurations for both fundamental and subharmonic mixers are also proposed and examined.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave MMIC characterization by noncontact electro-optic sampling
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The first time-domain measurements on millimeter-wave monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC) have been accomplished using noncontact electro-optic sampling. The technique, employing a tiny crystal of lithium tantalate, allows the extraction of voltage waveforms from arbitrary locations in integrated circuits. One study, of a Texas Instruments MMIC amplifier, has determined the response of a narrow-band circuit to have a center frequency of 32.5 GHz.

articleTitle: The NRL100 GHz carm oscillator experiment
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The design of a 10-20 MW, 40 nsec cyclotron autoresonance maser is presented. The basic components of the CARM are a novel 600 kV, 200 A. field emission gun and a “whispering gallery” mode rippled wall cavity.

articleTitle: The high brightness synchrotron infrared facility at brookhaven national laboratory
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The high brightness infrared synchrotron radiation facility at the National Synchrotron Light Source, Brookhaven National Laboratory, was turned on in May 1987. We describe in detail the experimental facilities provided on this source from the near infrared to the millimeter region. Theoretical calculations indicate that this source should be 100 to 1000 times brighter than a black body source in the range 40μm to 1 cm. We will report preliminary measurements of the beam intensity and source characteristics.

articleTitle: Broadside coupled striplines and suspended substrate microstrip lines for millimetre-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper presents, for the first time, design models of broadside coupled striplines and suspended substrate microstriplines which can be implemented on personal computers. The models have been obtained from the results of conformal transformation on homogeneous striplines, equivalence of the odd-mode with the quasi TEM mode of covered microstripline and logarithmic regression of spectral domain results. The present models represent at least an order of magnitude improvement in the computation time relative to the present numerical techniques. The design models presented will therefore be vital for fast and accurate computer aided design and optimization of microwave and millimeter-wave filters, couplers, DC blocks, mixers and various other useful circuits.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-magneto spectroscopy on p-type gaas/ga(al)as hetero structures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As compared to n-type GaAs/Ga(Al)As hetero junctions, the corresponding p-type structures are by far neither as well understood nor thoroughly explored. The reasons for this are the complicated valence-band structure from the theoretical point of view and the relatively low mobility of the 2D-holes from the experimental side. As a matter of fact, the summary of experimental and theoretical results re-mained fragmentary and inconsistent, so that no direct criterion could be used to distinguish between the different modes established [1–4]. In the present study we present a complex set of submilimeter-magneto-transmission data up to 35 Tesla for different sample configurations and temperatures in context with a straight-on simulation of the data applying KUBO's formula [5] for the microscopic high-frequency conductivity in a realistic op-tical multi-layer system including inter-ference effects.

articleTitle: The measurements of millimeter-waves in an optically controlled semiconductor-insulator composite waveguide
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel composite millimeter waveguide consisting of silicon-on-alumina has been developed. Measurements of laser controlled phase shift and attenuation at 94 GHz have been successfully carried out with both CW Ar-ion and Nd:YAG picosecond laser.

articleTitle: High power gyrotron experiments
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band gyrotron oscillator powered by a compact pulseline accelerator has been operated using oscillator cavities with and without axial slots. The use of axial slots has been shown to suppress low starting current “whispering-gallery” modes, in particular modes of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m2</inf> type, allowing stable operation in a linearly-polarized TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf> mode. A peak power of 35 MW has been observed at 6% efficiency.

articleTitle: Amplitude scintillations measurement on a 40 GHz, 14 km link in an arid climate
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We report the results of scintillation measurement obtained in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for 40-GHz links. Three types of scintillations viz; dry, semi-wet and wet scintillation were observed and recorded. Statistical analysis as well as a comparison with similar results will be presented.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental research of nonradiative dielectric waveguide directional couplers
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A practical design of nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide directional couplers is presented. The dispersion characteristics of coupled NRD-guides and the scattering coefficients of NRD-guide directional couplers are studied as well as the transitions from metal rectangular waveguide to NRD-guide couplers. Experiments of 3-dB and 10-dB NRD-guide couplers in ka-band show that the couplers are of good performance and promise in millimeter-wave integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Study of valence band structure of silicon by ftir at liquid helium temperatures
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: IR absorption measurements of FZ grown and boron doped silicon single crystals at liquid helium temperatures by spectra amplification technique of FTIR, revealed the existance of three bands in the 3000–2800 cm region superimposed upon broad absorption by free carriers. Deconvolution of these bands further showed some other weak bands. These bands are attributed to transitions involving valence sub-bands and spin orbit splitting of silicon.

articleTitle: “Complex” molecular spectra and the physics of the molecule: The case of methanol
publicationTitle: 1987 Twelth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The recent development of high resolution techniques in the far infrared (FIR), based on the optically pumped molecular laser, allows very precise frequency measurements in the spectral region between 10 μm and 2 mm, which is extremely interesting for molecular spectroscopy.
